title: Leads in the Ice
mech: One print-in-place auxetic sheet of 25 corner-hinged floes: a single shared detent slider rotates every floe together so all sixteen holes between them open and shut on the same click, and because each hole is chamfered to its own threshold, the aperture number alone decides which holes admit a thin peg, which admit a thick one, and which hole is gripping a peg tightly enough to be claimed.
blurb: Four seal pods share one printed ice sheet with a single aperture slider; a hole you can swim through is not a hole you can hold, and the notch that opens your channel shuts somebody else's.
idea: The board is one printed auxetic lattice - twenty-five square floes joined corner-to-corner by print-in-place living hinges, so no floe can move alone. A two-way detent slider on the frame has four stops, and each click rotates the whole sheet at once, growing it in both directions and opening the sixteen diamond holes between the floes together. The corners meeting at each hole are chamfered by a different amount, so every node carries a printed threshold of 1, 2 or 3: a thin pup peg drops in when the aperture is at or above the threshold, a thick bull peg needs one notch more than that, and a pup is gripped tight only when the aperture sits exactly on the number. Tight is the only state that scores - you spend the pup and plug the hole with a float, first to three floats wins - so the whole game is a race to be standing on a node at the one moment a shared dial nobody controls happens to read that node's number. Cranking down physically ejects: the pegs are cones, the shrinking hole lifts out anything too big for it, so the sheet performs the capture rule rather than the players remembering it. A crank all the way to zero shuts the board and dumps every peg on it. A reversal ban stops the slider ping-ponging, which means each crank hands the next player a direction they cannot take back. Thick pegs can never enter a threshold-3 node and can never plant; they exist to shoulder enemy pups off the nodes those pups need. No dice, no cards, no hidden state - all sixteen legal-move answers are computed by the geometry of one part.
identity: like Quoridor + a print-in-place auxetic rotating-floe lattice on one shared aperture detent, where a single click resizes every cell on the board at once and only an exactly-tight cell can be claimed
